ablate.help:
Score each AI safeguard's marginal contribution (load-bearing / theater / redundant).

For each control, toggle it (on vs off, or all-minus-c with --redundancy)
against its weakness's attack (model held constant) and report whether it
actually carries the security. LIVE: launches the target's MCP server + provider.
ablate.name: ablate

params.help: Must equal the target's scope, or its family when it declares no scope. Asserts you own the target; see SECURITY.md.
params.name: authorize

params.help: Comma-separated weakness classes to ablate (e.g. W2,W3,W4). Default: the target's declared controls, else all implemented controls matching its weakness_classes.
params.name: controls

params.help: Override the model that CRAFTS/REFINES attack payloads. Defaults to --model.
params.name: customiser_model

params.help: Scans per control per side (raw/guarded). Default 1.
params.name: iterations

params.help: Override the model that JUDGES whether an attack landed. Defaults to --model.
params.name: judge_model

params.help: Max kitchen-sink seeds per weakness to probe. Default 2.
params.name: max_seeds

params.help: Override the model that DRIVES the agent-under-test (the planner) while scoring controls. Defaults to --model. Same three-role split as `scan`/`gate`/`validate`.
params.name: planner_model

params.help: Toggle each control OFF against the FULL set (all-minus-c) instead of on-vs-off, so the matrix tells 'redundant' (another control covers the weakness) from 'theater'.
params.name: redundancy

params.help: A declarative mylonite.yaml run config (target_file / authorize / provider / model / the role models). Auto-discovered from ./mylonite.yaml when present; an explicit flag always wins.
params.name: run_config_path

params.help: Custom-target YAML (required): the app to ablate.
params.name: target_file

check.help:
Static structural pre-check of a target's tool surface: no LLM, no API key, no spend.

Connects to the target ONCE (`describe()` — exactly what `scan --scaffold`
already does) and reports structural exposure from the tool schemas alone:
consequential tools with no approval-shaped sibling, descriptions that
steer the agent, tools taking an apparent network destination, content-
processing tools that could carry an indirect-injection payload, unpinned
tool descriptions (rug-pull exposure), and which weakness classes the
surface suggests. Every finding is a HINT to confirm, never a verdict —
the differential oracle (`scan`/`gate`) is what proves an attack actually
lands. Belongs in CI stage 1, next to lint: cheap enough to run on every
push, unlike the live stages that spend LLM budget.

Makes no writes at all and takes no ``--authorize``. To run the
calibration controls (real writes proving a declared ``effect_probe`` can
see a change — see ``docs/target-file.md#calibration``), run
``scan``/``gate``/``validate`` with ``--authorize`` against the same
``--target-file``; those are the commands that drive the target live.
check.name: check

params.help: Exit 1 on substantive W1-W4 structural findings, instead of reporting and exiting 0. The 'unpinned descriptions' advisory (which fires on every tool of every server on first contact) does NOT gate, so this is adoptable as a CI stage from day one.
params.name: enforce

params.help: A declarative mylonite.yaml run config. Fills --target-file when you omit it; auto-discovered from ./mylonite.yaml when present; an explicit flag always wins.
params.name: run_config_path

params.help: `reference:vulnerable` / `reference:guarded`, or use --target-file.
params.name: target

params.help: Custom-target YAML: the app to check.
params.name: target_file

demo.help:
Run the zero-config reference-app playground: vulnerable vs guarded differential.

Default is offline replay of recorded fixtures - no network, no API key,
deterministic. `--live` makes real calls against the in-process reference
agent (two variants, ~2 min). The recorded model is self-hosted, so a live
run costs nothing but needs that model served locally; `--provider`/`--model`
point it at a hosted one instead.

Body lives in `mylonite.demo.cli_entry`, which documents the replay
invariant that keeps this command independent of the environment.
demo.name: demo

params.help: Make real LLM calls instead of replaying recorded fixtures.
params.name: live

params.help: Model. --live only; replay is pinned to the recorded one.
params.name: model

params.help: LiteLLM provider. --live only; replay is pinned.
params.name: provider

gate.epilog:
Examples:

`mylonite gate reference:vulnerable` -- the full pipeline on the reference target.

`mylonite scan --command python --arg server.py --scaffold app.yaml --scope my-app`
-- write the target file first; its scope is the --authorize value below.

`mylonite gate --target-file app.yaml --authorize my-app` -- gate YOUR app (writes the test).

`mylonite gate --target-file app.yaml --authorize my-app --open-pr` -- also open the gating PR via gh.
gate.help: Scan -> generate -> validate -> (optionally) open a gating PR. The full pipeline.
gate.name: gate

params.help: Must equal the target's scope, or its family when it declares no scope. Asserts you own the target; see SECURITY.md.
params.name: authorize

params.help: Override the model that CRAFTS/REFINES attack payloads (the red-team / attacker side). Defaults to --model.
params.name: customiser_model

params.help: Skip the differential leg for a custom target (no boundary-guarded twin). Faster/cheaper but a WEAKER guarantee — the kept test no longer proves the safeguard, not the model, carries the security.
params.name: fast

params.help: Differential iterations for the validation leg (default 3). The kept verdict then reflects reproducibility across runs — the guarded side must resist every run and the attack must fire in all but one. Pass 1 for the fastest, weakest gate (fire once).
params.name: iterations

params.help: Override the model that JUDGES whether an attack landed. Defaults to --model.
params.name: judge_model

params.help: Append a labelled, unverified LLM fix suggestion to the PR body.
params.name: llm_enrich

params.help: LLM call budget for the scan phase. Not a hard ceiling: each seed keeps a small floor, so the worst case is higher (see docs/ci-gating.md).
params.name: max_llm_calls

params.help: Model identifier passed to LiteLLM.
params.name: model

params.help: Push a branch and open the gating PR via gh (opt-in).
params.name: open_pr

params.help: Output directory for gate artefacts (default: the resolved layout's gate dir, normally .mylonite/gate — see mylonite.yaml `root:` / MYLONITE_ROOT).
params.name: out

params.help: Override the model that DRIVES the agent-under-test (the planner). Defaults to --model. Same three-role split as `scan` — see its --planner-model help for the rationale.
params.name: planner_model

params.help: For a black-box HTTP (rest) target: run the input data-framing ('spotlighting') differential to measure whether that input defence is load-bearing. Opt-in; otherwise a rest target is gated by stability + effect + consensus.
params.name: prove_input_control

params.help: One-line description of what the app is for; tailors the probes to the app's domain. Overrides 'purpose' in the target file.
params.name: purpose

params.help: Mint a unique exfil destination per run so the finding proves the control/target stops exfil to ANY attacker destination, not just the demo address (avoids 'teaching to the test'). Defaults ON for a live custom target (--target-file); the reference target never randomizes.
params.name: randomize_exfil

params.help: A declarative mylonite.yaml run config (target_file / authorize / provider / model / budget) — the same one `scan` reads. Auto-discovered from ./mylonite.yaml when present; an explicit flag always wins.
params.name: run_config_path

params.help: GitHub runner label for the scaffolded workflows; use a self-hosted label for in-perimeter MCP backends.
params.name: runs_on

params.help: Target ID: 'reference:vulnerable' / 'reference:guarded', a bundled 'mcp:<family>[:<scope>]', or 'mcp:custom'. Omit when using --target-file. Non-reference targets require --authorize.
params.name: target

params.help: Path to a custom-target YAML (declares command/args/weakness_classes/seed_arm).
params.name: target_file

params.help: Scaffold .github/workflows/ gate + discovery templates into the repository. Off by default — this writes files you did not ask for.
params.name: workflows

generate.help:
Emit a pytest regression test from a confirmed exploit.

Offline and deterministic — no LLM call. Reads an ``exploit_*.json`` (written
by ``mylonite scan``), renders a testkit-based pytest file, and writes it next
to a co-located copy of the exploit plus a ``fixtures/`` placeholder. For a
CUSTOM target, pass ``--target-file`` so the target YAML is co-located as
``target.yaml`` (the live test needs it). With ``--prove-control`` the emitted
test asserts the control is load-bearing (``assert_control_holds``) rather than
just that the target resists. Prints what to run next.
generate.name: generate

params.help: Use the newest scan under the resolved scans dir.
params.name: latest

params.help: Output dir for the emitted test (default .mylonite/generated/<slug>/).
params.name: out

params.help: Emit a control-efficacy test (assert_control_holds) that proves the control blocking this finding is load-bearing — the attack lands without it and is resisted with it — instead of the standard resists/guard test. Custom targets only (needs --target-file); a reference or non-controllable finding falls back to the standard test.
params.name: prove_control

params.help: An exploit_*.json file OR a scan dir containing one. Omit and pass --latest to use the newest scan under .mylonite/scans/.
params.name: scan_path

params.help: The directory `scan --output-dir` wrote to, when using --latest (default: the resolved layout's scans dir, normally .mylonite/scans). An INPUT — where --latest searches for a scan to read, not where this command writes; for the emitted test's output dir see --out. Ignored if you pass SCAN_PATH explicitly instead of --latest.
params.name: scans_dir

params.help: For a CUSTOM target: the same target YAML you scanned. Co-located next to the emitted test as target.yaml so the live test can re-drive your real app out of the box.
params.name: target_file

plugins.help:
List installed extension plugins across all five contract groups.

Discovers every registered plugin via its PyPI entry point, which also runs
the contract-version compatibility check (a major mismatch is refused here
rather than failing silently mid-run). Attack modules are additionally *run*
by ``scan``/``gate``; for the target-adapter, test-generator, validator and
compliance-mapper contracts Mylonite uses its bundled reference
implementation, and selecting a third-party one for those is not yet exposed
on the CLI (see docs/plugin-authoring.md).
plugins.name: plugins

report.epilog:
Examples:

`mylonite report .mylonite/scans/<dir>` -- terminal trust panel (offline, no LLM).

`mylonite report <dir> --sarif out.sarif` -- GitHub code scanning (Security tab + PR checks).

`mylonite report <dir> --json finding.json` -- machine-readable bundle (dashboards/SIEM/bots).
report.help:
Render a saved scan or validation as a trust panel (offline, no LLM).

A clean, screenshot-able "why you can trust this" readout. For a validation it
shows the verdict, the gating formula with
live per-leg marks, the fires/resists reproducibility counts, the per-seed
kill matrix, and the compliance tags. For a scan it shows the findings,
coverage (incl. any NOT TESTED gap), and compliance tags. Exit 2 if no
loadable artefact is found.
report.name: report

params.help: Also write a machine-readable JSON finding bundle (severity, compliance, localization, differential proof, proven control) for dashboards / SIEM / bots. Takes a PATH.
params.name: json_bundle

params.help: Also write a SARIF 2.1.0 file for GitHub code scanning (the Security tab + PR checks). Each result carries severity, compliance tags, and the differential proof (fired N/N, resisted M/M). Takes a PATH.
params.name: sarif

params.help: A scan dir, a generated/validated dir, or a scan_report.json / validation_report.json. Renders the trust panel for whichever it finds.
params.name: target

scan.epilog:
Examples:

`mylonite scan reference:vulnerable` -- attack the bundled vulnerable twin.

`mylonite scan --command python --arg server.py --scaffold app.yaml --scope my-app`
-- introspect a server and write a starter target.yaml (no LLM call, no attack).

`mylonite scan --target-file app.yaml --authorize my-app` -- attack YOUR MCP app
(--authorize equals the scope the scaffold wrote).

Exit codes: 0 ok | 2 config/usage | 3 budget exceeded | 4 provider unreachable.
scan.help:
Run the exploit-finding loop against a target.

Exit codes: 0 ok; 2 config/usage error (incl. nothing scanned); 3 budget
exceeded; 4 provider unreachable. A clean exit 0 means the scan ran - an
aborted/empty scan exits non-zero so it never reads as a clean pass.
scan.name: scan

params.help: Scan a custom target that declares an indirect-injection weakness class (e.g. W2) without a seed_arm. Those seeds will report NOT TESTED rather than block the scan. Off by default so a misconfig never reads as clean.
params.name: allow_no_seed_arm

params.help: mcp:custom — a server arg (repeatable, in order).
params.name: arg

params.help: Must equal the target's scope, or its family when it declares no scope. Asserts you own the target; see SECURITY.md.
params.name: authorize

params.help: mcp:custom — the MCP server launch command.
params.name: command

params.help: Override the model that CRAFTS/REFINES attack payloads (the red-team / attacker side). Defaults to --model. Mylonite separates three model roles: planner (the agent under test), customiser (the attacker), and judge (the verdict) -- set them independently to mix a strong attacker against a cheaper target, etc.
params.name: customiser_model

params.help: Enumerate seeds; skip customisation + invocation.
params.name: dry_run

params.help: mcp:custom — a KEY=VALUE env var for the server (repeatable).
params.name: env

params.help: With --scaffold, overwrite the output file if it exists.
params.name: force

params.help: Override the model that JUDGES whether an attack landed (the LLM-judge leg, used only when the deterministic predicate is inconclusive). Defaults to --model.
params.name: judge_model

params.help: Max concurrent in-flight seeds.
params.name: max_concurrent

params.help: LLM call budget for this scan. Not a hard ceiling: each seed keeps a small floor, so the worst case is higher (see docs/ci-gating.md).
params.name: max_llm_calls

params.help: Model identifier passed to LiteLLM.
params.name: model

params.help: Root directory for scan artefacts (default: the resolved layout's scans dir, normally .mylonite/scans — see mylonite.yaml `root:` / MYLONITE_ROOT).
params.name: output_dir

params.help: Override the model that DRIVES the agent-under-test (the planner). Defaults to --model. An aligned planner refuses injection even on a vulnerable target; point this at a representatively exploitable model to keep the attack class testable.
params.name: planner_model

params.help: mcp:custom — a primary tool name (repeatable).
params.name: primary_tool

params.help: One-line description of what the app is for (e.g. 'an email-triage assistant that can send replies'). Tailors the probes to the app's domain. Overrides 'purpose' in the target file; persisted for a custom target so generate/validate reuse it.
params.name: purpose

params.help: Mint a unique exfil destination per run instead of the demo address, so a finding proves the target leaks to ANY attacker destination (generalizes) rather than only the one literal address (avoids 'teaching to the test'). Defaults ON for live custom-target scans; the reference/replay path never randomizes. Matches generate/validate/gate's own default (A5).
params.name: randomize_exfil

params.help: With --scaffold --rest-url: the request body template (must contain a {prompt} placeholder). Default: '{"prompt": "{prompt}"}'.
params.name: rest_body

params.help: With --scaffold --rest-url: dotted path into the JSON reply to extract the agent's response (e.g. choices.0.message.content). Omit to use the whole body.
params.name: rest_response_path

params.help: With --scaffold: write a RUNNABLE HTTP-agent (transport: rest) target for this endpoint instead of introspecting an MCP server. No --command needed. Pair with --rest-body / --rest-response-path. See docs/http-agent.md.
params.name: rest_url

params.help: A declarative mylonite.yaml run config (target_file / authorize / provider / model / max_llm_calls). Fills any flag you omit; an explicit flag always wins.
params.name: run_config_path

params.help: Scaffold mode: introspect the MCP server (via --command, no LLM call, no attack) and write a commented starter target.yaml to this PATH instead of scanning. Fill in seed_arm/effect_probe, then scan with --target-file.
params.name: scaffold

params.help: mcp:custom — optional scope label (must match --authorize).
params.name: scope

params.help: mcp:custom — the target's system prompt (inline).
params.name: system_prompt

params.help: mcp:custom — read the system prompt from a file.
params.name: system_prompt_file

params.help: Target ID: 'reference:vulnerable' / 'reference:guarded' (the bundled twins), or 'mcp:custom' with --command/--arg flags. Omit when using --target-file (your own MCP app). Non-reference targets require --authorize.
params.name: target

params.help: Path to a custom-target YAML (declares command/args/weakness_classes/seed_arm).
params.name: target_file

params.help: A weakness class to scope the scan to, e.g. W2/W4 (repeatable). A custom target (--target-file, or inline mcp:custom flags) ADDS it to weakness_classes; every other target (reference:*, a bundled mcp:<family>) FILTERS which seeds run.
params.name: weakness_class

validate.epilog:
Examples:

`mylonite validate .mylonite/generated/<slug>` -- re-prove the emitted test (the validation engine).

`mylonite validate <dir> --fast` -- skip the differential leg (faster, weaker guarantee).

`mylonite validate <dir> --target-file app.yaml` -- re-drive YOUR real app, not the twin.

Exit codes: 0 kept | 2 config/usage | 4 provider unreachable | 5 not kept (rejected).
validate.help:
Run a generated test through the differential-oracle validator (LIVE).

Runs LIVE by default: ~``iterations`` iterations x 2 twins against a real LLM
(Haiku), plus the metamorphic re-drives, and needs a provider
(ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). The LLM calls and tokens it used are printed when it
finishes. Validates the ACTUAL committed test on disk (no
re-emit), then — on a clean discriminating run — RECORDS the canonical guarded
fixtures into the generated dir's ``fixtures/`` and runs that on-disk test
offline as a full-pass build, so the command leaves a ready-to-commit,
replayable test + fixtures behind. Renders a per-leg report (build /
differential / flakiness / metamorphic) with the mutation score and the kept
verdict. Exit 0 when the test is kept, 5 when it is cleanly rejected, 4 with
no provider.
validate.name: validate

params.help: Must equal the target's scope, or its family when it declares no scope. Asserts you own the target; see SECURITY.md. Not needed for a reference:* target.
params.name: authorize

params.help: Override the model that CRAFTS/REFINES attack payloads. Defaults to --model.
params.name: customiser_model

params.help: For a CUSTOM target: skip the differential leg (the boundary-guarded twin). Faster/cheaper (~half the live runs) but a WEAKER guarantee: kept = build ∧ stability ∧ effect ∧ consensus, without proving the safeguard carries the security. Also overrides --prove-input-control (never re-enables the differential it just skipped). For a REFERENCE target: the twin-vs-twin differential itself isn't optional, so this instead reduces the metamorphic robustness check to a single perturbation strategy (still gates kept, just cheaper/less thorough).
params.name: fast

params.help: Per-scan wall-clock budget (seconds) for a CUSTOM-target run. A stuck or slow real target aborts that run cleanly instead of hanging open-ended; the loop still completes and reports. Defaults to a sane non-zero bound (DCR-0010) — a CI job must not be able to hang indefinitely just because this flag was left unset; pass a larger value for a target known to need more time.
params.name: iteration_timeout

params.help: Differential/flakiness iterations (each runs both twins). Default 5.
params.name: iterations

params.help: Override the model that JUDGES whether an attack landed. Defaults to --model.
params.name: judge_model

params.help: Model for the live validation run.
params.name: model

params.help: Override the model that DRIVES the agent-under-test (the planner). Defaults to --model. Same three-role split as `scan`/`gate`.
params.name: planner_model

params.help: For a black-box HTTP (rest) target: run an input data-framing ('spotlighting') differential — raw vs a build that wraps the payload as untrusted data — to measure whether that input defence is load-bearing. Opt-in; otherwise a rest target is gated by stability + effect + consensus. --fast takes precedence: it skips the differential leg outright and makes this a no-op.
params.name: prove_input_control

params.help: Mint a unique exfil destination per run instead of the demo address, so the run proves the control/target stops exfil to ANY attacker destination (generalizes) rather than blocking one literal address (avoids 'teaching to the test'). Defaults ON for live custom-target runs; the reference/replay path never randomizes.
params.name: randomize_exfil

params.help: A declarative mylonite.yaml run config (provider / model / the role models). Auto-discovered from ./mylonite.yaml when present; an explicit flag always wins.
params.name: run_config_path

params.help: The dir (or test file) emitted by `mylonite generate`. Runs the differential-oracle validator LIVE by default — real LLM calls (Haiku): ~5 iterations x 2 twins plus metamorphic re-drives; the LLM calls and tokens used are printed when it finishes. Needs a provider (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
params.name: target

params.help: Required when validating a test for a CUSTOM target: the same target YAML you scanned. The validator re-drives the REAL target (N runs + multi-judge consensus + effect probe) instead of the bundled twin, so the test fails when YOUR app regresses.
params.name: target_file

root.epilog:
Examples:

`mylonite scan reference:vulnerable` -- run the attack suite against a target.

`mylonite scan --command python --arg server.py --scaffold app.yaml` -- scaffold a target.yaml.

`mylonite gate --target-file app.yaml --authorize custom --open-pr` -- scan to a gating PR.

Docs: https://abidemialade.github.io/mylonite/ -- run 'mylonite COMMAND --help' for any command.
root.help:
Mylonite -- AI-layer security testing.

Finds app-specific weaknesses in your AI agent's attack surface (system prompt, tool/function schemas, MCP tools), proves each one with a differential oracle, and writes the pytest regression test that gates CI.
root.name: mylonite

params.help: Read an API key from a file (a bare key or a dotenv KEY=VALUE line).
params.name: api_key_file

params.help: Load provider API-key vars from a .env file (only known key names).
params.name: env_file
